transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

I start projects and assignments full of ideas, but I just can’t seem to follow through and finish things, and it’s already cost me my first job. I'm here because I really need to understand why I can't seem to complete tasks reliably despite my best intentions.
Have you often had trouble paying attention, been easily distracted, or felt restless and fidgety since childhood, even when you wanted to focus?

Yes, this definitely goes back to childhood; my elementary report cards always said I was "bright but daydreams," and I constantly lost worksheets and got in trouble for talking out of turn. Even now, I'm easily pulled off task by a roommate walking past or just a random thought, and I get this constant "buzzing" restless feeling under my skin whenever I have to sit still.
Do you often feel the need to move around, like tapping your hands or feet, or feel impatient and restless, especially during tasks that require sustained attention?

Yes, I'm constantly fidgeting, shaking my leg, or pacing because sitting still for more than a few minutes feels almost unbearable. I get this buzzing sensation under my skin, and my friends even joke that I have an internal motor that doesn't have an off switch. Even when I try to just relax and watch a show, I can't seem to stay quiet and still.

This is characteristic of conditions involving impaired executive functioning, particularly inattention and poor task completion. The primary differential at this stage includes disorders marked by these symptoms, with F90.0 (Hyperkinetic disorder) being the most consistent with the described pattern of chronic underachievement due to inattention and impulsivity, despite motivation. No other specific symptoms (e.g., mood episodes, psychosis, anxiety) have been reported yet, so the candidate list remains focused on neurodevelopmental origins.
